profile.objective: Determine which sales figures can support a valuation and which contracts and cash records are still needed.
profile.model_rationale: Juniper bills for subscriptions. Two accounts have paid. The records do not identify how much each has committed to renew.
profile.scope: The fictional case includes a sales ledger, a registration extract and three pricing records.

documents.name: Juniper subscription and cost ledger
documents.reviewed: Two paying accounts, annual revenue of USD 100,000 and direct costs of USD 40,000.
documents.limitations: The ledger does not separate recurring fees from other charges or state the renewal terms.

documents.name: Juniper registration extract
documents.reviewed: Registered name of the operating company.
documents.limitations: The extract does not identify the owners of the software, customer contracts or other operating assets.

documents.name: Juniper introductory pricing release
documents.reviewed: The company advertised a USD 40 entry price.
documents.limitations: The release omits the offer end date and what the entry tier includes.

documents.name: Independent review of entry subscription offers
documents.reviewed: An independent analyst recorded a USD 55 entry offer.
documents.limitations: The offer dates and package differ from the USD 40 release, preventing a like-for-like comparison.

documents.name: Reprint of Juniper introductory terms
documents.reviewed: The publisher reproduced the company’s USD 40 offer.
documents.limitations: The reprint traces to the same company release and adds no independent price observation.

evidence.title: Juniper subscription and cost ledger
evidence.extract: Dated invoices and collection records identify two paid subscription users. The synthetic year to cut-off reports revenue of USD 100,000 and COGS of USD 40,000.

evidence.title: Juniper registration extract
evidence.extract: The registration extract identifies Juniper Workflows Demo Co and the registered name.

evidence.title: Juniper introductory pricing release
evidence.extract: The preserved release gives a USD 40 entry price, without tier scope or offer end date.

evidence.title: Independent review of entry subscription offers
evidence.extract: The analyst's captured offer lists a USD 55 entry price. The package terms and offer dates differ.

evidence.title: Reprint of Juniper introductory terms
evidence.extract: This reprint quotes the same USD 40 company release verbatim.

claims.statement: The accounting packet reports USD 100,000 in recognised revenue.
The entry price is USD 40 per month.
claims.rationale: Tiers and effective dates mismatch, so the exact comparable price remains unresolved.

thesis.management: Subscription demand should translate into a predictable recurring-revenue business.
thesis.independent: Two paid accounts establish initial demand. Their recurring contract value, renewals and Juniper’s cash balance are unknown.
falsifiers: Independently reconciled paid cohorts that show stable renewal and collectible, comparable prices.

divergences.impact: Withhold a matched entry price and any peer inference that depends on it.

safeguards.rationale: The scope of this fixture is defined by the supplied packet.

factors.question: Which legal entity owns the product, contracts and securities?
factors.finding: The registry identifies Juniper Workflows Demo Co. The extract says nothing about software title, contracting parties or issued shares.
factors.impact: A valuation could be assigned to an entity that does not hold the operating rights.
factors.next_test: Match signed customer contracts and IP assignments to the issuer and reconcile its share register.

factors.question: Who has demonstrated demand or willingness to pay for the current offer?
factors.finding: The ledger identifies two paying accounts. Their use and renewals are undocumented.
factors.impact: Those payments establish initial demand from two buyers. Wider adoption is unknown.
factors.next_test: Review dated usage and renewal decisions for each account.

factors.question: What can the team deliver at the evidenced stage?
factors.finding: The invoices identify no feature delivered or accepted by a customer.
factors.impact: Revenue alone cannot establish what Juniper can deliver repeatedly.
factors.next_test: Match an invoice to the product version, delivery record and customer acceptance.

factors.question: Who controls delivery and decisions, and what track record is evidenced?
factors.finding: None of the five documents identifies who leads sales, product delivery or finance.
factors.impact: A handover or key-person dependency cannot be evaluated.
factors.next_test: Request role histories and a reference for a prior delivery.

factors.question: Which alternatives compete for the same buyer and budget?
factors.finding: Juniper lists USD 40 per month. An independent review lists USD 55 under different terms. The newsletter repeats Juniper’s release.
factors.impact: The two figures cannot establish a like-for-like starting price.
factors.next_test: Align offer dates, included features and term lengths.

factors.question: What drives recognised revenue and contribution at the current stage?
factors.finding: The ledger reports USD 100,000 revenue and USD 40,000 direct costs. It gives no split between recurring and one-time sales.
factors.impact: Reported gross margin is 60%. Contribution per account remains unknown.
factors.next_test: Reconcile revenue and direct costs by account and charge type.

factors.question: Which dated cash and funding constraints affect the next decision?
factors.finding: The ledger contains sales and costs. It contains no unrestricted cash balance or forward commitments.
factors.impact: The funding date and cash available for reinvestment are unknown.
factors.next_test: Obtain a dated bank reconciliation and monthly cash commitments.

factors.question: What evidence suggests an advantage can survive replication or switching?
factors.finding: The documents record payments but no reason a customer renewed, switched or stayed.
factors.impact: The valuation cannot assume high switching costs.
factors.next_test: Ask both customers about alternatives and check their renewal decisions.

factors.question: Which operational, regulatory or other dependencies could prevent delivery?
factors.finding: No operating agreements identify Juniper’s hosting or delivery dependencies.
factors.impact: The cost or interruption caused by a supplier change is unknown.
factors.next_test: Review the main hosting agreement and service commitments to customers.

factors.question: What observable change would invalidate the independent case or valuation basis?
factors.finding: There is no supported forecast, cash bridge or priced comparable transaction.
factors.impact: A change in renewal assumptions could reverse the valuation case.
factors.next_test: Reconcile paid renewals and build a forecast that separates existing and new customers.

factors.question: What is the defendable value basis, method and sensitivity at the cut-off date?
factors.finding: The records cover operating sales and product prices. They contain no transaction value or supported cash forecast.
factors.impact: Neither a transaction multiple nor a discounted cash-flow range is available.
factors.next_test: Source dated enterprise values with comparable revenues and reconcile the forecast cash flows.

factors.question: How much contracted recurring revenue is evidenced and reconcilable?
factors.finding: Two accounts paid. The ledger gives no signed term, recurring charge or invoice-line split for either.
factors.impact: Contracted monthly recurring revenue and ARR are unknown.
factors.next_test: Match signed subscriptions to recurring invoice lines, excluding one-time charges and credits.

factors.question: What do mature cohort retention and acquisition costs show?
factors.finding: Opening cohorts, renewals and acquisition spend are missing.
factors.impact: Customer retention and payback cannot be estimated.
factors.next_test: Trace both accounts through renewal and match acquisition spend to new accounts.

factors.question: Is initial revenue collectible and repeatable beyond the first customers?
factors.finding: Two accounts made payments. No renewal record shows a second contract term or how collections change beyond these accounts.
factors.impact: The receipts establish initial sales. Their repeatability is still open.
factors.next_test: Check subsequent collections and renewal dates against the two signed agreements.

research.reason: The extract confirms the registered name. It contains no share register, IP assignment or signed customer agreement.
The ledger identifies two paid accounts and total annual sales and costs. It has no invoice split or contract schedule from which to calculate recurring revenue.
The newsletter copies the USD 40 release. The independent USD 55 offer covers different terms.
Cash statements and a supported cash-flow forecast are unavailable in this packet.
The ledger documents transactions but gives limited evidence of sustained product usage.
Checking employment history requires web access and the packet has no biographies.
Current cohorts and churn data must come from the company.
All four ordinary reviews were used on the ledger, registration and price dispute. Supplier terms were outside those documents.

inputs.label: Reported revenue
inputs.rationale: Reported in the subscription and cost ledger for the year ended 27 November 2026.

inputs.label: Reported cost of goods sold
inputs.rationale: Reported in the subscription and cost ledger for the year ended 27 November 2026.

valuations.rationale: There is no comparable enterprise transaction price or matched revenue denominator.

challenges.finding: Company release and independent price review disagree.
challenges.correction: Retain both sources and request dated plan inclusions.

gaps.item: Reconciled cash statement and valuation driver schedule
gaps.period: At 27 November 2026 and monthly over the forecast
gaps.why: The packet does not establish unrestricted cash, affordable reinvestment or a defensible forecast.
gaps.conclusion: The date Juniper needs funding and the cash flows available for valuation.
gaps.action: Reconcile the cash balance and forecast drivers, and retest method eligibility.

gaps.item: Dated like-for-like subscription offers and tier terms
gaps.period: Both offers in force at 27 November 2026
gaps.why: Recorded pricing disagrees and the copied release is one origin.
gaps.conclusion: Whether USD 40 and USD 55 are comparable entry prices for the same contract.
gaps.action: Align dates and included features before using pricing in comparables.

gaps.item: Dated customer cohorts and churn reconciliation
gaps.period: From each account’s first invoice through its latest renewal opportunity
gaps.why: The ledger does not describe renewals or switching.
gaps.conclusion: Whether customers renew and how much growth must come from acquiring new accounts.
gaps.action: Test retention and switching behaviour by customer vintage.

gaps.item: Signed customer agreements, software IP assignments and issued-share register
gaps.why: The registry names the company but identifies none of these rights.
gaps.conclusion: Which entity owns the operating assets, earns the contract receipts and issues the shares.
gaps.action: Match each agreement and assignment to the registered entity and reconcile the securities.

gaps.item: Subscription terms, invoice lines and credits for the two paying accounts
gaps.period: The reported year and each contract’s current term
gaps.why: Annual recognised sales combine charges with unknown recurrence.
gaps.conclusion: How much contracted revenue can enter the valuation and which sales have been collected or renewed.
gaps.action: Tie recurring charges to enforceable terms, separate one-time items, and reconcile receipts and direct costs.

gaps.item: Dated comparable transaction prices and matched company revenue
gaps.why: Subscription list prices measure what users pay. They do not establish the enterprise price paid for a business.
gaps.conclusion: Whether a revenue multiple can support an enterprise valuation.
gaps.action: Match enterprise value and revenue period, accounting and business mix before calculating a multiple.

decision.conclusion: Withhold a valuation range. Two customers paid, but their contract terms and recurring billings are unknown. Total annual revenue cannot serve as contracted recurring revenue.
decision.limitations: The five fictional documents cover one accounting year and two paid accounts. Web research and outreach were unavailable.
strengths: Reported revenue of USD 100,000 less USD 40,000 in direct costs gives a 60% gross margin (E1).
risks: The public offers give conflicting entry prices. A cash balance, forward costs and comparable transaction prices are also missing.

research_plan.objective_rationale: Determine whether the signed subscription and cash evidence support a defensible valuation basis.
research_plan.stage_rationale: Dated receipts identify two paying accounts. There is no renewal history.
research_plan.limitations: Only frozen synthetic packet records were reviewed. Web research and outreach were unavailable.

questions.question: Which legal entity owns the product, contracts and securities?
questions.evidence_required: Dated registration, ownership and entity perimeter matched to the assessed business.
questions.counter_test: Check similarly named entities, former names and mismatch between invoices, product and fundraising entity.
questions.decision_use: Establish the entity, ownership, and transaction eligibility.

questions.question: How much contracted recurring revenue is evidenced and reconcilable?
questions.evidence_required: Subscription ledger, period and bridge excluding one-offs, bookings and implementation income.
questions.counter_test: Trace churn, pauses, reclassifications and annualisation of non-recurring receipts.
questions.decision_use: Set the recurring revenue base for valuation and growth.

questions.question: Which alternatives compete for the same buyer and budget?
questions.evidence_required: Comparable offers and buyer substitution evidence matched by segment, geography, period and unit.
questions.counter_test: Look for private or manual substitutes, old price lists and scope mismatches.
questions.decision_use: Assess market access, price position and adoption alternatives.

questions.question: Which dated cash and funding constraints affect the next decision?
questions.evidence_required: Unrestricted cash, commitments, cash movement and timing or a precise request for the missing records.
questions.counter_test: Test restricted cash, delayed collections and conditional finance against the same timeline.
questions.decision_use: Determine funding needs, liquidity exposure and timing.

questions.question: Who has demonstrated demand or willingness to pay for the current offer?
questions.evidence_required: Segment-specific demand evidence that distinguishes interest, use, purchase and repeat use.
questions.counter_test: Find inactive users, rejected offers, unpaid pilots and alternatives purchasers already use.
questions.decision_use: Test demand and reachable customer segments.

questions.question: Who controls delivery and decisions, and what track record is evidenced?
questions.evidence_required: Named responsibilities, relevant execution history and decision rights.
questions.counter_test: Check contradictory biographies, conflicts and departures that change who can deliver.
questions.decision_use: Assess execution, governance and key-person dependencies.

questions.question: What evidence suggests an advantage can survive replication or switching?
questions.evidence_required: Customer behaviour, protected rights or operational economics that can be traced to the advantage.
questions.counter_test: Identify reproducible features, weak IP coverage, multi-homing and low switching costs.
questions.decision_use: Test durability and the persistence of value drivers.

questions.question: Which supplier or operating agreement could restrict customer delivery?
questions.evidence_required: A scoped dependency and compliance record for the entity, geography and actual operations.
questions.counter_test: Check scope limits, expired or conditional permissions, and any reliance on an uncommitted third party.
questions.decision_use: Identify conditions that could block operations or invalidate the decision.
